Lower Right Triangle Symbol

There is no legacy Windows Alt code for Lower Right Triangle because it is not in either the OEM code page 437 or Windows-1252 tables. The Unicode codepoint is U+25FF, which you can use as ◿ in HTML, \25FF in CSS, or type with Alt+9727 on Windows (BMP only). If your keyboard has no numeric keypad, use the Character Viewer, the HTML entity, or copy the character directly. Lower Right Triangle is outside both legacy code pages, which is why U+25FF is the identifier that works across Word, HTML, CSS, Python and JavaScript. Lower Right Triangle has no named HTML entity, so use the numeric escape ◿ or the hex escape ◿.

How to type lower right triangle on Windows

  1. Turn Num Lock on so the numeric keypad is active.
  2. Hold the left Alt key.
  3. Type 9 7 2 7 on the numeric keypad for the decimal codepoint 9727.
  4. Release Alt. The Lower Right Triangle character (◿) appears.

If your keyboard has no numeric keypad, see how to type symbols without a numpad.

How to type lower right triangle on macOS

There is no direct Option shortcut for Lower Right Triangle. Open the Character Viewer with ⌃⌘Space, search for "Lower Right Triangle" and click the character to insert it.

How to use lower right triangle in code

  • HTML: or
  • CSS: content:"\25FF"; ()
  • Python: \u25FF or chr(0x25FF)
  • JavaScript: \u25FF or String.fromCodePoint(0x25FF)
  • JSON: "\u25FF"

Frequently asked questions

Is there an Alt code for ◿?

No legacy Alt code exists for Lower Right Triangle because it is not in code page 437 or Windows-1252. Use the Unicode codepoint U+25FF in HTML, CSS or the Character Viewer instead.

How do I type ◿ without a numpad?

Use the Windows Character Viewer (Win+.), the macOS Character Viewer (⌃⌘Space), an HTML entity such as ◿, or copy the character directly from this page.

Why does Alt+9727 not work?

Alt+9727 only works on a keyboard with a physical numeric keypad. It also requires the application to accept the numeric-keypad input path. Laptops without a numpad need an alternative method.

What is the Unicode for Lower Right Triangle?

The Unicode codepoint for Lower Right Triangle is U+25FF. You can use this value in HTML as ◿, in CSS as \25FF, and in Word with Alt+X.

How do I type ◿ on a Mac?

Open the Character Viewer with ⌃⌘Space and search for the character name or U+25FF, then click it.
